articles.title: Costco is getting a new kind of member
articles.summary: The company recently shared an exciting update that highlights an interesting trend.
articles.body:
When you think of your typical Costco member, you probably picture someone like me — a frazzled, sweatpants-clad suburban mom with unbrushed hair whose cart is loaded with snacks, eggs, milk, and more tissue boxes than she can count.

But it's not just hot-mess moms you'll see roaming the warehouse club aisles these days.

Costco is attracting a younger generation of shoppers.

And the warehouse club retailer believes the demographic shift could be an important driver of future growth.

Costco is attracting a younger generation

During Costco's fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call , CFO Gary Millerchip highlighted the younger shopper trend, pointing to the growing number of members under age 40.

"What we've also been pleased with in that membership growth is seeing a younger member and sort of seeing that penetration go through over a quarter now of all members being under 40, we think is a really positive sign to your point about continued growth in spend per member," Millerchip said .

The milestone suggests Costco is finding ways to appeal to shoppers who may have different habits and expectations than the generations that helped build its business.

It also offers a potential opportunity to establish long-term relationships with consumers who could remain members for decades.

Costco's membership model is central to its business. So it wants to attract as many young shoppers as it can to boost that revenue stream.

Younger members can benefit, too. Costco's food offerings, gasoline prices, and private-label Kirkland Signature products give shoppers of all ages many ways to offset the cost of membership while reaping value.

Of course, one thing that distinguishes younger shoppers is their tendency to make purchases online or using apps.

That's an area where Costco has been improving.

Costco has invested in its digital capabilities, giving customers additional ways to browse products and shop beyond its physical warehouses.

The company reported record levels of digital engagement during fiscal 2026, according to comments from management on the earnings call.

Costco also highlighted strong engagement among its Executive members, who generally spend more than customers with its standard Gold Star membership.

Those trends matter because Costco wants its members to do more than sign up. It wants them to shop frequently, spend more over time, and renew their memberships year after year.

Attracting younger customers could help Costco sustain that pattern, particularly as those new members move through different stages of life, from living independently to raising families and buying homes.

articles.title: Dólar opera em alta, com foco em inflação americana e cenário político brasileiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Na véspera, a moeda americana avançou 0,71%, cotada a R$ 5,0198. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 1,04%, aos 206.888 pontos
articles.summary: Na véspera, a moeda americana avançou 0,71%, cotada a R$ 5,0198. Já a bolsa brasileira recuou 1,04%, aos 206.888 pontos
articles.body:
O dólar opera em alta nesta quarta-feira (14), com um avanço de 0,29% perto das 9h50, cotado a R$ 5,0346 . Já as negociações do Ibovespa , principal índice da bolsa brasileira, começam às 10h.

Os novos dados da inflação americana e a divulgação do Livro Bege, do Federal Reserve ( Fed , o banco central dos Estados Unidos ) são o principal destaque da agenda econômica de hoje. No noticiário nacional, investidores seguem atentos ao andamento da PEC que propõe o fim da escala 6x1 no Senado e à nova pesquisa eleitoral Quaest, prevista para às 18h.

▶️ No Brasil, o cenário político segue no radar. Ao longo do dia, o destaque fica com a votação da PEC que prevê o fim da escala 6x1, que enfrenta nesta quarta-feira uma das votações mais importantes de sua tramitação no Congresso Nacional. Entenda o que está em jogo.

▶️ Já no quadro eleitoral, a Quaest divulga, após o fechamento do mercado, sua primeira pesquisa de intenção de voto para o 2º turno. A pesquisa também deve trazer votos no primeiro turno, nívei de rejeição aos candidatos, conhecimento sobre propostas dos presidenciáveis e avaliação do governo Lula.

▶️ Já na agenda econômica, o foco fica com o índice de preços ao consumidor (IPC) dos EUA. O indicador, que mede a inflação ao consumidor americano, subiu 0,6% em setembro, em uma aceleração em relação ao observado em agosto (0,4%) e em linha com o esperado pelo mercado.

Os dados reforçam a expectativa de alta dos juros pelo Fed em sua próxima reunião, no fim deste mês. Juros mais altos nos EUA tendem a fortalecer o dólar e a afastar investidores de mercados emergentes, como o Brasil, além de aumentar a pressão para a manutenção dos juros elevados por aqui.

▶️ O livro Bege do Fed também fica sob os holofotes. O relatório reúne relatos de empresas e especialistas para mostrar como está a atividade econômica em diferentes regiões dos Estados Unidos e pode trazer pistas sobre quais os próximos passos da instituição na condução dos juros americanos.

Veja abaixo mais detalhes do dia no mercado.

Na Ásia , as ações chinesas encerraram a sessão desta quarta-feira no nível mais baixos em mais de um ano, à medida que a onda de vendas de ações relacionadas à cadeia de suprimentos de inteligência artificial se intensificava e conforme investidores repercutiam os novos dados de inflação do país.

O SSEC , índice de Xangai, caiu 0,9%, enquanto o CSI300 , índice que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzen, recuou 1,4%. Entre os demais índices da região, o Nikkei , do Japão, perdeu 0,05% e o Hang Seng , de Hong Kong, desvalorizou 0,1%. O Kospi , da Coreia do Sul, teve perdas de 0,44%.

* Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters.

articles.title: Manuel Belmar recebe reconhecimento concedido pelo MIPCOM e pela ONU à Agenda ESG da Globo | G1
articles.standfirst: Homenagem será entregue durante o MIPCOM, em Cannes, e destaca iniciativas da empresa na área ambiental e o papel do conteúdo audiovisual na promoção de debates sociais.
articles.summary: Homenagem será entregue durante o MIPCOM, em Cannes, e destaca iniciativas da empresa na área ambiental e o papel do conteúdo audiovisual na promoção de debates sociais.
articles.body:
Conecta ESG Jundiaí 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

A Globo recebeu, nesta quarta-feira (14), em Cannes, na França, o MIPCOM Recognition for SDG Impact, reconhecimento concedido em parceria com a Organização das Nações Unidas ( ONU ) pela contribuição da empresa aos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS).

A homenagem destaca o potencial do conteúdo audiovisual para promover debates sociais e ambientais, além das iniciativas de sustentabilidade adotadas pela companhia em suas operações.

Manuel Belmar, diretor de Finanças (CFO) da Globo e líder da agenda ESG — sigla em inglês para ambiental, social e governança — da empresa, recebeu o reconhecimento durante o MIPCOM, um dos principais eventos internacionais da indústria audiovisual.

"Na Globo, nosso impacto está no conteúdo que produzimos, nas conversas que ajudamos a mobilizar, nas vozes e perspectivas que levamos ao público e na forma como conduzimos o negócio. A Agenda ESG conecta essa influência a ações concretas em nossas operações e na indústria audiovisual. Este reconhecimento reforça nossa responsabilidade de seguir usando nosso alcance para contribuir com uma sociedade mais inclusiva e para um setor cada vez mais sustentável", afirmou Belmar durante a homenagem, em Cannes.

A homenagem faz parte de uma parceria entre o MIPCOM e a ONU, que chega ao oitavo ano. A iniciativa também está ligada ao Pacto de Mídia pelos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS), criado em 2018 e que reúne mais de 450 empresas de mídia e entretenimento em 160 países.

O reconhecimento considera a atuação da Globo na promoção de questões como diversidade, redução das desigualdades, educação e fortalecimento das instituições democráticas, além de iniciativas ambientais.

Paulo Marinho, diretor-presidente da Globo, destacou a importância da conquista. "ESG não é uma área na Globo, mas uma atuação transversal a todo o negócio. Este reconhecimento é resultado de um trabalho consistente que mobiliza toda a empresa e que tem em Manuel Belmar uma liderança fundamental. Ao longo dos últimos anos, ele ajudou a consolidar uma Agenda ESG que conecta propósito e negócio, transforma compromissos em ações concretas e amplia o impacto positivo que podemos gerar por meio do nosso conteúdo, das nossas operações e da nossa relação com a sociedade. Esta homenagem do MIPCOM e da ONU reconhece essa visão e o trabalho diário de centenas de profissionais que fazem essa agenda avançar em toda a empresa", disse.

🔍 As empresas participantes usam seus canais de comunicação para divulgar temas relacionados aos 17 objetivos globais da ONU, que incluem o combate à pobreza e à desigualdade, a proteção do meio ambiente, o enfrentamento das mudanças climáticas e a promoção da paz e da justiça.

A empresa também ampliou a adoção de práticas sustentáveis em produções audiovisuais por meio do Guia de Produções Verdes.

Outra iniciativa é a Ecovision, parceria com a Panvision que busca ampliar a adoção de práticas sustentáveis no setor audiovisual latino-americano.

O impacto das produções da Globo também se reflete fora das telas. Na novela Vale Tudo, uma cena em que a personagem Lucimar, interpretada pela atriz Ingrid Gaigher, recorre a um aplicativo da Defensoria Pública do Rio de Janeiro para formalizar a guarda do filho e cobrar pensão alimentícia foi seguida por um aumento na procura pelo serviço.

Na mesma novela, a abordagem da dependência de álcool por meio da personagem Heleninha Roitman, interpretada por Paolla Oliveira, também repercutiu fora da ficção.

As buscas pelos canais oficiais dos Alcoólicos Anônimos (AA) aumentaram mais de 150%, de acordo com dados divulgados à época.

Realizado anualmente em Cannes, na França, o MIPCOM reúne emissoras de televisão, plataformas de streaming, produtoras e distribuidoras de diversos países para apresentar conteúdos, negociar formatos e estabelecer parcerias comerciais.

A Globo participa do evento há décadas e apresenta suas produções ao mercado audiovisual internacional.

articles.title: Benito Arruñada, economista: "El principal especulador, con muchísima diferencia, son las administraciones públicas"
articles.standfirst: El economista critica los impuestos que gravan la vivienda nueva
articles.summary: El economista critica los impuestos que gravan la vivienda nueva
articles.body: La vivienda vuelve a ocupar el centro del debate político en España. El Gobierno ha aprobado nuevos decretos para intervenir en el mercado inmobiliario, reforzar la protección de los inquilinos y ampliar la oferta de vivienda asequible. Las medidas han reavivado la discusión sobre cómo frenar el encarecimiento de los alquileres y qué responsabilidad tienen las administraciones públicas en el problema. En este contexto, una declaración del economista Benito Arruñada, realizada hace más de dos años, vuelve a poner sobre la mesa una de las cuestiones más controvertidas: el papel del Estado en el precio de la vivienda. "El principal especulador, con muchísima diferencia, son las administraciones públicas", afirmó Arruñada en junio de 2024. El catedrático de Organización de Empresas de la Universidad Pompeu Fabra cuestionaba así la fiscalidad que grava la vivienda, especialmente los impuestos asociados a la construcción y a la compraventa de inmuebles. Su argumento se centraba en que la carga tributaria contribuye a elevar el coste final de la vivienda nueva. Una crítica que cobra actualidad en un momento en el que el Ejecutivo vuelve a impulsar medidas para facilitar el acceso a un hogar y limitar determinadas prácticas del mercado inmobiliario. El pasado 6 de octubre, el Consejo de Ministros aprobó dos nuevos reales decretos-ley con medidas relacionadas con el alquiler, la fiscalidad y la oferta de vivienda. Entre otras actuaciones, el paquete incluye una prórroga extraordinaria de hasta dos años para determinados contratos de alquiler, límites a la actualización de las rentas y cambios fiscales destinados a favorecer el uso residencial de los inmuebles. Las normas están en vigor, aunque deben ser convalidadas por la Diputación Permanente del Congreso tras la disolución de las Cortes. La crítica de Arruñada apunta a uno de los elementos que intervienen en el precio de una vivienda: los impuestos. En su planteamiento, los gravámenes asociados a las transmisiones inmobiliarias y a la construcción tienen un efecto sobre el coste que acaba soportando el comprador. El economista defendía revisar ese modelo fiscal y reducir la carga que soportan determinadas operaciones inmobiliarias. Su postura forma parte de un debate más amplio sobre las causas de la crisis residencial, en el que conviven diagnósticos distintos: desde quienes ponen el foco en la falta de oferta y las dificultades para construir hasta quienes reclaman una intervención pública más intensa para contener los precios y ampliar el parque de vivienda asequible. La fiscalidad inmobiliaria en España no se limita a los impuestos que pagan los propietarios por tener una vivienda o alquilarla. La construcción y la compraventa de inmuebles también están sujetas a distintos tributos que repercuten en el coste final de las operaciones. En el caso de la vivienda nueva, el comprador paga, con carácter general, un 10% de IVA sobre el precio de adquisición. El tipo se reduce al 4% para determinadas viviendas de protección oficial de régimen especial o de promoción pública. Además, la formalización de la compraventa puede estar sujeta al Impuesto sobre Actos Jurídicos Documentados (AJD), cuyo tipo depende de la comunidad autónoma. En las viviendas de segunda mano, en cambio, el comprador paga el Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales (ITP), que también depende de la comunidad autónoma en la que se encuentre el inmueble. Este tributo grava la transmisión de la vivienda y supone un coste adicional para quien la adquiere. La construcción también soporta impuestos. Las obras de construcción o rehabilitación de edificios destinados principalmente a viviendas tributan, con carácter general, al 10% de IVA cuando se cumplen los requisitos legales. A ello pueden sumarse tributos y tasas municipales, como el Impuesto sobre Construcciones, Instalaciones y Obras (ICIO), que grava la realización de determinadas obras y cuyo tipo depende de cada ayuntamiento. Los dos reales decretos aprobados por el Gobierno en octubre de 2026 incorporan medidas fiscales vinculadas a la vivienda, pero no establecen una reforma general del IVA aplicable a la compra de vivienda nueva ni del ITP que grava las viviendas usadas. Tampoco suprimen con carácter general el AJD asociado a determinadas operaciones inmobiliarias. Por tanto, la carga fiscal que soportan estas operaciones sigue siendo un elemento central del debate sobre el precio de la vivienda, aunque su impacto concreto varía según el tipo de inmueble, la operación y la comunidad autónoma.

articles.title: India-US trade deal nearing finish line? What Jaishankar, Piyush Goyal said on negotiations and ties
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has said that India and the United States were continuing talks to resolve differences over the proposed
articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has said that India and the United States were continuing talks to resolve differences over the proposed trade deal, adding that negotiations appeared to be heading towards a “landing point”.He also said the core fundamentals of the bilateral strategic partnership remained unchanged. “I think we are waiting on a few things. I wouldn't be comfortable spilling the beans in public,” Jaishankar said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Tuesday evening when asked about the status of negotiations, PTI reported.“When countries negotiate with an economy like the United States, obviously one part of it is what you work out between yourselves and the US, and one part of it is how do you fare vis-a-vis competitive economies,” he added.He said the outcome would also depend on the terms other countries secured in their negotiations with Washington.“And that part of it is not entirely clear because not everybody has worked out a deal. I think people, the trade ministers, USTR (US Trade Representative) there and our Commerce and industry minister are there working on that. They're ironing it out,” he said.“My sense is that this is an issue which is heading towards a landing point,” Jaishankar added.His remarks came more than a week after finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said negotiations on the India-US trade agreement had reached a “plateau”.Goyal says India-US ties are ‘very good’Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said India-US relations were “very good” and would continue to improve regardless of changes in political thinking in either country.“Of course, it is already very good. I don't see any problem as we speak also. And to my mind, the relationship with the US that India enjoys is very substantive, very consequential for the world, being two large democracies,” Goyal said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Wednesday.He was responding to a question on whether bilateral relations would improve after US President Donald Trump leaves office.Goyal said the relationship extended beyond trade to defence, technology, critical minerals and people-to-people ties.“One must bear in mind that we have, it's not only about trade, which of course they are our largest trading partner and I think will continue to be in the years to come. And by and large, I don't see any problem in any agreements also with the United States,” he said.Goyal added, “It's about trade, it's about defence partnership, it's our technology partnership, it's our critical minerals partnership, it's our people-to-people engagement”.He said both countries continued to engage closely on defence exercises and efforts to maintain open supply chains for technology, goods and services.“The US and India have a very, very consequential relationship and it's only going to get better irrespective of changes in political thinking, whether in India or in the US. The relationship draws its strength from our economic imperatives, from our political imperatives, from our security imperatives,” he said.“So it's a very safe relationship. I don't think the rest of the world needs to worry about it,” he added.India and the US have been negotiating a proposed bilateral trade pact since early 2025 to address tariff-related tensions, remove non-tariff barriers and improve market access.India is seeking more favourable tariff terms for its exports to the US compared with those offered to competing economies.Earlier this month, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the two countries were working to finalise a trade deal, but an agreement was not imminent. He said both sides had identified the outstanding issues and were working towards resolving them.'We are not officially an ally'Jaishankar said Washington's approach to economic engagement had changed, with tariffs forming part of a broader effort to revive domestic manufacturing and reset access to the US market.“The US has a fundamentally different approach to the use of tariffs. But even that is a symptom of something else. The US is today determined to re-industrialise and to reset the terms of access to its economy,” he said.“That's what the whole tariff debate is about. And the two are connected: access to the American economy and the re-industrialisation of America. Therefore, what is happening is every significant economy is getting into a negotiation with the United States on this issue,” he added.Jaishankar said India was not alone in negotiating with Washington and that its discussions were at an advanced stage. “We're not alone in this. In our case, we are pretty far advanced in that process of negotiation,” he said.Jaishankar also discussed Washington's changing approach to alliances and treaty relationships, saying the impact was being felt most strongly in Europe and, to some extent, in East Asia.He said India’s relationship with the US was different because the two countries were strategic partners, not formal allies.“We have many issues we are working on with the United States, but we don't have an issue of the terms of alliance because we are not officially an ally.""We are a country which has a strong strategic partnership with the US, but a strategic partnership is a partnership; it's not an alliance,” he added.Jaishankar said the two countries had spent more than two decades identifying areas of convergence and shared interests.“In our case, for the last 20-odd years, we have worked out what we felt were convergences, overlaps, shared common interests with the US, and we had agreed that we would pursue that. I don't think that has fundamentally changed,” he added.India-US relations have faced a downturn following Washington's imposition of punitive tariffs on Indian goods last year.Changes to US immigration policy and an increase in H-1B visa fees further strained ties.Relations came under fresh pressure after Washington moved to restrict a key green-card processing programme affecting major global and Indian IT firms, including Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro.Despite the tariff pressures, India's exports to the US rose marginally by 0.92% to $87.3 billion in the 2025-26 fiscal year. Imports from the US increased 15.95% to $52.9 billion. As a result, India's trade surplus with the US narrowed to $34.4 billion in 2025-26 from $40.89 billion in 2024-25.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, sobre la posibilidad de que Rufián sea el líder de Podemos: “El control siempre será de Pablo Iglesias”
articles.standfirst: El experto considera que si se unen serían un desafío para Frente Amplio
articles.summary: El experto considera que si se unen serían un desafío para Frente Amplio
articles.body: Podemos no será parte del Frente Amplio. Tras el anuncio de que Ada Colau será la líder de la coalición de partidos, el grupo liderado por Ione Belarra e Irene Montero decidió salirse de la ecuación. De momento, esta formación está integrada por Izquierda Unida (UI), Sumar, Más Madrid y los comunes. Es decir, tampoco está ERC con Gabriel Rufián al frente. Es por eso que en las últimas horas se ha sellado una alianza entre Podemos y ERC. Después de los halagos que Rufián y Montero intercambiaron en el pasado, era una posibilidad. Ambos partidos reconocen estar abiertos a más alianzas: “Se puede incorporar quien quiera”. Pero, por ahora, harán “equipo” para las elecciones. Lo que se sabe del pacto entre la formación morada y ERC es que Podemos ayudará a los independentistas en la región catalana y, a cambio, Rufián será uno de los rostros más habituales en los actos de campaña de Irene Montero. Esto provoca, en primer lugar, que el liderazgo a nivel nacional quede un poco difuso. De hecho, de ello ha hablado el economista Gonzalo Bernardos en su cuenta de X. “¿Qué está pasando en la extrema izquierda?”, se pregunta el experto financiero. Después de las últimas decisiones, llega a la conclusión de que “no tienen cómo objetivo volver a gobernar (lo han descartado)”, sino que buscan dar respuesta a “quién es la formación hegemónica”. Bernardos es consciente de que con la ayuda de Rufián, “Podemos desafía a Frente Amplio”. Ahora bien, no atribuye esta táctica ni al propio político de ERC ni a los vigentes en la formación morada. “Es una hábil maniobra de Iglesias”, advierte. De todos modos, en su opinión, no importa quien sea la cara visible del proyecto, pues el liderazgo de Podemos está en la sombra: “En el futuro, ¿será Rufián el nuevo líder de Podemos? El líder puede ser cualquiera, pero el control de la empresa familiar siempre lo llevará la misma persona: Pablo Iglesias”.

articles.title: Woman applied for 130 IPO shares, bank entered only 65; consumer commission awards Rs 37,000 for deficient service but rejects her Rs 40 lakh compensation claim
articles.summary: You apply for a certain number of shares for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) and then discover that the bank has recorded only half of the number!
articles.body: You apply for a certain number of shares for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) and then discover that the bank has recorded only half of the number! What do you do in such a case where there is a cut in the potential size of your allotment?This is what a woman, an Ahmedabad resident, faced. She claimed the bank's mistake caused her a loss of Rs 42,142 and sought a compensation of Rs 40 lakh.What the case is aboutIn 2022, the woman applied for 130 shares in an IPO. However, the bank recorded her application for just 65 shares, which she claimed resulted in a loss of Rs 42,142. She also accused the bank of causing her physical and mental harassment.Also Read | Rs 5.89 crore FD interest slashed from 7.75% to 3.5% without notice; Delhi High Court rejects bank’s non-renewal argument and orders interest at an average of earlier ratesThe woman initially took her complaint to the Ahmedabad District Consumer Commission, but her appeal was dismissed. She subsequently approached the Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. The state commission heard the matter and ruled in her favour, though it granted her only partial relief.The woman claimed that the discrepancy resulted from an error by the bank, which, according to her, acknowledged the mistake in an official communication.Representing his wife, her husband argued that the bank could not escape responsibility by dismissing the mistake as “typographical” or “clerical”. He also submitted that her account had sufficient funds to cover the IPO application. Had the bank entered the correct number of shares, he argued, she would have been allotted 130 shares.“A data-entry or clerical error committed by a bank employee, if it results in financial loss to the customer or deprives the customer of a financial benefit, cannot be treated as an ordinary or significant mistake,” her counsel argued according to an ET report, citing ICICI Bank vs Santosh Sardana (2021).The bank’s counsel argued that the transaction was intended to facilitate an investment in shares with the objective of earning a profit. On that basis, the lawyer maintained that it was a commercial activity and the woman did not meet the definition of a ‘consumer’.“Share trading is a commercial activity and an investor is not a “consumer” within the meaning of the Consumer Protection Act”, the bank’s counsel said.Also Read | She worked as a teacher till 62 years of age instead of retiring at 60, but was denied gratuity because of extended service; Allahabad HC orders payment with 6% interestThe bank's lawyer also contended that the Ahmedabad District Consumer Commission was right to conclude that the woman had not furnished proof of payment of consideration to the bank. According to the counsel, she had also failed to provide documentary evidence showing that she was entitled to an allotment of 130 shares and had lost that entitlement because of the bank's alleged mistake.The District Commission rejected her complaint on the ground that she did not qualify as a consumer. It held that investing in shares amounted to a commercial activity and, consequently, the complaint was not maintainable, Supriya Majumdar, Partner at Elarra Law Offices, told ET.The Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission subsequently partly allowed the woman’s appeal.Also Read | Sisters sought share in parents’ properties under Hindu Succession law; Madras HC rules for brother over mother’s land on ouster, father’s estate over missing partiesWhy did the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission provide some relief?After considering the arguments from both sides, the Gujarat State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission held that the woman could be considered a beneficiary of the bank's services. It said that the fact that she had not directly paid the bank did not, by itself, conclusively establish that she was not a consumer.The commission also observed that a transaction involving shares does not automatically make every dispute concerning banking services associated with an IPO a commercial dispute. Therefore, the woman could not be denied the right to seek redressal against the bank merely because her complaint arose from an IPO application.“Banking institutions are required to maintain a reasonable degree of care, accuracy, and diligence when processing applications and entering customer-related information,” the commission stated according to the ET report.However, the commission did not agree with the woman’s claim that she had suffered a loss of Rs 42,142. It also rejected her demand for Rs 40 lakh in compensation, describing the amount as “highly excessive”.Instead, the commission directed the bank to pay her:Rs 20,000 for deficiency in service.Rs 10,000 for mental agony and harassment.Rs 7,000 towards the costs of the original proceedings and the present appeal.The total amount payable to the woman was therefore Rs 37,000.Supriya Majumdar said the woman succeeded in her appeal on two counts: the maintainability of her complaint and the deficiency in the services provided by the bank.During the appeal, the complainant also submitted a SEBI circular to argue that banks providing IPO-related services were entitled to receive charges or compensation from another institution or entity.“Thus, although the complainant may not have personally paid any consideration to the bank, the circular indicated that the IPO-related service was not necessarily a service rendered entirely without consideration, as the bank was entitled to receive compensation,” she explained.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claimsThe commission rejected the claimed financial loss because allotment in an IPO is governed by prescribed procedures and subscription ratios. Consequently, assuming that the woman would certainly have received all 130 shares was speculative.Majumdar emphasised that, although the bank had admitted entering an incorrect number of shares in the application, the woman had not established that the error caused her a loss of Rs 42,142.Her claim depended on the “assumption” that she would necessarily have been allotted 130 shares had the application been recorded correctly, rather than on concrete evidence demonstrating that outcome.For this reason, the commission declined to award the Rs 40 lakh compensation she had sought.Also Read | Man paid Rs 1.73 crore for Gurgaon flat, waited over a decade without possession; builder alleges homebuyer bought it for commercial gain, consumer commission awards refund with 12% interest & Rs 4 lakhYou use AI every day. articles.title: From Chinese money laundering to Russia, Iran sanctions - why was Bank of America fined $1.21 billion?
articles.summary: Bank of America has been fined $1.21 billion by US regulators for failing to detect and report billions of dollars in suspicious transactions, including
articles.body: Bank of America has been fined $1.21 billion by US regulators for failing to detect and report billions of dollars in suspicious transactions, including activity linked to potential money laundering and sanctions violations.The US treasury department said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious activity, including $1 billion that posed national security-related and other illicit finance risks. The unreported activity included transactions that may have involved Chinese money laundering networks and trade-based laundering linked to the US southwest border, according to the Treasury.The department said the bank prioritised revenue while building its compliance programmes and relied too heavily on inquiries from law enforcement and other financial institutions rather than its own internal controls. This effectively outsourced a substantial part of its responsibility to proactively detect and report suspicious activity, it said.Violated Bank Secrecy ActAs part of the settlement, Bank of America admitted that it had “willfully violated” the Bank Secrecy Act by failing to maintain a compliant anti-money laundering programme, conduct required due diligence on foreign correspondent accounts and file suspicious activity reports, the Treasury said.The $1.21 billion penalty includes a $750 million civil fine imposed by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the largest in the regulator’s history. The OCC said the bank had failed to address shortcomings in its anti-money laundering programmes identified in a 2024 cease-and-desist order. It described the bank’s compliance programme as “deficient and ineffective” and said its transaction monitoring system had delayed reports covering billions of dollars in transactions.The bank also agreed to pay $11.6 million to the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) over 475 apparent violations of sanctions programmes targeting Russia, Iran, narcotics and global terrorism. OFAC said the settlement reflected its determination that the apparent violations were “non-egregious”.Under the settlement, the bank must hire an independent third party to review past transactions, identify suspicious activity it failed to detect and report those transactions to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).Bank of America said it had invested billions of dollars in technology and dedicated thousands of employees to fighting financial crime. It added that it was committed to completing the work required by regulators and had already devoted substantial personnel and resources to remediation.The bank said its third-quarter results, due on Wednesday, would include a non-tax-deductible charge of $1.2 billion, reducing net income by approximately 17 cents per share.The penalty comes days after American Express was fined $350 million for similar anti-money laundering shortcomings. Bank of America shares fell 2.7% in after-hours trading on Tuesday, after closing down 1.1%.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Making progress': Taiwan on Alaska LNG deal after Trump says it will buy 30% of output
articles.summary: Taiwan said on Wednesday it was making progress in negotiations to buy liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Alaska and planned to invest up to $4.4 billion in
articles.body: Taiwan said on Wednesday it was making progress in negotiations to buy liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Alaska and planned to invest up to $4.4 billion in the project. The announcement came after US President Donald Trump said Taiwan had agreed to buy 30% of the proposed project's output.Taiwan's economy ministry said state-owned energy company CPC Corp had made significant progress with the project developer after nearly 18 months of negotiations and evaluation.Under the plan, CPC would purchase 6 million metric tonnes of LNG annually once production begins, in line with a letter of intent signed last year.The company would also participate in the project's development, with an estimated investment of up to $4.4 billion, the ministry said, Reuters reported."Specific investment arrangements, equity stakes and related terms will be determined through subsequent negotiations and commercial contract procedures," it added.However, the final investment terms and purchase commitments remain subject to further negotiations and commercial agreements.Taiwan has been looking to increase purchases of US natural gas and reduce its dependence on other suppliers. Earlier in February, officials said US gas would account for about one-third of the island's imported supply this year.The proposed Alaska LNG project is designed to export up to 20 million metric tonnes of LNG annually. The project has been discussed for decades, but its commercial viability remains a concern for some industry experts.If completed, the pipeline would provide a direct route for US LNG to Asian markets, including Taiwan, without requiring shipments to pass through the Panama Canal or travel around the Horn of Africa. This could reduce shipping times and costs.The move is also part of Taiwan's effort to narrow its large trade surplus with the United States, which has angered the Trump administration.CPC signed an agreement with the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation last year to buy LNG and invest in the project. Alaska's governor said in March 2025 that Taiwan had signed a letter of intent to purchase 6 million metric tonnes annually.Taiwan President Lai Ching-te had said the investment would help strengthen the island's energy security.Last year, Taiwan Presidential Office Secretary-General Pan Men-an also visited the proposed project site in Alaska as the Trump administration promoted the project to Asian allies.Trump at a rally in Alaska on Tuesday said that Taiwan had agreed to buy 30% of the project's output.US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who attended the event organised by the Republican National Committee, said Taiwan had committed $4.4 billion towards the pipeline's development.Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai, responding to Trump's remarks said the government's responsibility was to "stabilize the entire energy supply and build its resilience, like governments everywhere."The announcement did not establish whether a final, binding agreement had been signed. Taiwan's economy ministry said the investment arrangements and equity stakes would be settled through further negotiations.Last month, Trump said South Korea had agreed to invest in the Alaska LNG project, which he valued at $54 billion. Seoul, however, said the proposed investment had not yet been finalised.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: China’s exports surge amid AI-driven demand
articles.summary: Exports grew by 36.3 percent in September, the biggest leap since the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.body:
China’s exports surged by more than one-third in September, a boost to the world’s second-largest economy as it faces slowing growth.

Exports grew by 36.3 percent last month year-on-year to reach $447.18bn, accelerating from a 25 percent gain in August, government figures released on Wednesday show.

The leap marked the biggest monthly rise in exports since 2021, when China’s trade figures were skewed by the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and stringent lockdowns.

Tech-related trade led the growth, with semiconductor exports surging more than 108 percent and shipments of automatic data processing machines jumping nearly 55 percent.

Imports increased 31 percent year-on-year, up from 28.2 percent in August, according to the figures from the General Administration of Customs.

“High-tech demand, supported by the global and domestic AI upcycle, remained the key driver, while China’s pricing and supply-chain competitiveness in other major export categories also helped sustain the momentum,” Taylor Wang, an economist at HSBC in Hong Kong, said in a note to clients.

China’s total exports in the first nine months of the year rose 21.3 percent to $3.37 trillion, while imports gained 27.5 percent to $2.43 trillion.

The gap between exports and imports in the first three quarters gave China a trade surplus of $938.1bn.

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was China’s biggest export market by a wide margin, with exports rising more than 52 percent in September to $81.7bn.

Exports to the European Union rose 25.3 percent in September to $60.15bn, while shipments to the United States jumped 39.6 percent to $47.88bn.

After decades of relying on state-led investment and exports to power its economy, China is striving to find new avenues for growth amid a falling population, deflating property market, and weak domestic consumption, which contributes far less to gross domestic product (GDP) than in advanced economies.

China’s economy is expected to grow 4.5 percent in 2026, according to the International Monetary Fund’s latest growth outlook, which would be the slowest expansion since 1990, excluding the outlier years of the COVID pandemic.

“The strong export growth should keep China’s growth on track to achieve its growth target of 4.5-5 percent for 2026,” Lynn Song, chief economist for Greater China at ING, told Al Jazeera.

“Nonetheless, growth remains quite unbalanced, with domestic data quite soft in comparison,” Song said.

“It will be important to rebalance growth over the medium term if China is to achieve its longterm growth targets.”

articles.title: Why Elon Musk is liking Micron right now

articles.body:
X chatter is calling it a "bull posting" from Elon Musk on AI stock darling Micron ( MU ).

"Micron has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate, which is something today's customers won't forget… Micron is making is the smart move for long-term customer loyalty," Musk said in a new X post .

Not that Micron needed more hype; it's doing just fine making that happen on its own.

Micron blew it out of the water on its earnings day several weeks ago. Crushed it on every single line item. And with guidance.

Consider this: Micron added about $43 billion in sales during the most recent quarter compared to the year-ago quarter. It added more than $13 billion in sales from the quarter reported three months ago. All of this is massive.

Operating margins exploded in all business segments. In fact, operating margins are over 80% in some segments.

What's more, Micron execs signal tight capacity and higher prices for its products until 2028.

Last week, the company announced it has raised its stock repurchase authorization to $35.16 billion. The company is able to start buying back stock on Dec. 9 once CHIPS Act restrictions lift.

"New technology, divestiture of non-core assets, and cost-cutting efforts should help it improve gross margins and profitability in the coming quarters," JP Morgan analyst Harlan Sur said.

articles.title: India working to rebuild ties with China, but future remains uncertain: Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday said India was working to rebuild its relations with China, while stressing that the future
articles.body: Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday said India was working to rebuild its relations with China, while stressing that the future of the engagement remained open.He also said India was willing to enter into joint ventures with any country, provided it received a fair deal and there was continuity in engagement.“We are open to all countries around the world as long as we get a fair deal, as long as we ensure continuity in the engagement, and as long as the geopolitical situation does not deteriorate. I think we had some concerns in the past. We are working to develop relations with China once again, but the last word has not yet been scripted on this journey,” Goyal said at the Bloomberg New Economy event, according to news agency PTI.His remarks come as China remains India's second-largest trading partner, with bilateral trade increasing in the last financial year even as the trade deficit widened.India-China trade grows, deficit widensBilateral trade between India and China rose 7.9% to $151.10 billion in 2025-26, up from $118.39 billion in 2024-25.India's exports to China grew 36.62% to $19.47 billion during the last fiscal year, compared with $14.25 billion a year earlier. Imports from China increased 16% to $131.62 billion.India's trade deficit with China widened to $112.16 billion in 2025-26 from $99.21 billion in the previous financial year. The deficit remains an area of concern for India.Investment is another issue in bilateral ties. India has tightened its foreign direct investment (FDI) policy for countries that share a land border with it, including China.Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Chinese President Xi Jinping on September 12, on the sidelines of the Brics Summit.Goyal flags supply-chain vulnerabilitiesSpeaking about the broader geopolitical environment, Goyal said partnerships with other countries would become increasingly important.“Everybody has recognised the importance of friends, and that's going to be the most important critical element in the years to come,” he said.Recalling the Covid-19 pandemic, the minister said India had focused on self-reliance after facing difficulties in securing essential supplies from other countries.He said India had provided food grains and vaccines to more than 100 countries during the pandemic, but had itself faced shortages when global supply chains were disrupted.“During Covid, we really recognised the vulnerabilities that a nation like India, a large nation of 1.4 billion people, had to go through when supply chains were broken. We did not get adequate material for meeting our needs during Covid. Wherever we had placed orders for personal protective equipment or Covid kits or vaccines, we were let down miserably by all countries,” Goyal said.He also alleged that Western countries had refused to supply vaccines made by Pfizer and Moderna to India.“When we needed Pfizer and Moderna vaccines, the West refused to give it to us... They even refused to make an application to get the vaccine into the Indian market, even though we were willing to waive all the conditions. So, it's a global phenomenon,” he said.Goyal said these experiences prompted Prime Minister Narendra Modi to give the call for Atmanirbhar Bharat, or self-reliant India.India and Singapore discuss semiconductor cooperationAt the same event, Singapore's deputy Prime Minister and minister for energy, trade and industry Gan Kim Yong said the two countries were discussing ways to strengthen India's semiconductor industry.“We are also working on training and skilling of the Indian workforce so that we can support the growth of semiconductors,” he said, according to PTI.The India-Singapore trade pact came into force in 2005.Goyal also spoke about India-US relations at the event, describing the partnership as substantive and saying it would improve regardless of changes in political thinking in either country.He said the relationship extended beyond trade to defence, technology, critical minerals and people-to-people ties.The two countries are also negotiating a bilateral trade agreement, with discussions continuing over market access and tariffs.You use AI every day. articles.standfirst: El catedrático reflexiona sobre el impacto de los nuevos vehículos
articles.summary: El catedrático reflexiona sobre el impacto de los nuevos vehículos
articles.body: El coche eléctrico gana cada vez más terreno en el mercado. En un contexto en el que el petróleo está en el centro de conflictos bélicos y tensiones geopolíticas, como la crisis del estrecho de Ormuz, su impacto en la economía se incrementa. El catedrático Santiago Niño Becerra ha reflexionado en sus redes sociales sobre el efecto que tiene esta tecnología en las finanzas de los países importadores del combustible fósil. "20.000 millones de dólares es mucho dinero teniendo en cuenta el nivel de mentalización actual y los escasos meses en que esa cantidad se ha generado. Pienso que es un tema para meditar, discutir y decidir", ha planteado el economista en su cuenta personal de X, antes Twitter. Santiago Niño Becerra ha publicado esta reflexión citando un artículo de El País sobre el impacto de la crisis energética provocada por el conflicto en el estrecho de Ormuz. El citado artículo hace referencia al último informe de Ember Energy, en el que se concreta que China, por el crecimiento del vehículo eléctrico, se ha ahorrado 14.000 millones de dólares y la Unión Europea, 3.100 millones de dólares. En la UE, Alemania (760.000) y Francia (560.000) son los que más han notado el impacto de este cambio de tendencia. Este informe señala, además, que la venta de vehículos eléctricos ha subido a lo largo de 2026. De hecho, esto se ha producido en 49 de los 56 países analizados en el estudio. La aceleración en las ventas de vehículos eléctricos a raíz de la crisis en el estrecho de Ormuz fue especialmente destacable en India, Chile, Australia y Nueva Zelanda. Ember Energy también apunta que en Estados Unidos las ventas de coches eléctricos se han estancado y quince países de todo el mundo han vendido más vehículos de este tipo que en el país dirigido por el presidente Donald Trump.

articles.title: In 2019, first Vande Bharat Express was rolled out from ICF; in 2026 RCF and MCF also manufacture semi-high speed train sets, with RCF-made Vande Bharat tested successfully at 180 kmph
articles.summary: Vande Bharat Express trains had till the start of this year been manufactured only at the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai.
articles.body: Vande Bharat Express trains had till the start of this year been manufactured only at the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai. However, in 2026 the other two Indian Railways’ coach factories - Rail Coach factory (RCF) Kapurthala and Modern Coach Factory rolled out their first Vande Bharat Express trains.And now the 16-coach Vande Bharat Chair Car train set which has been manufactured at RCF Kapurthala has successfully been tested at speeds of 180 kilometres per hour.The train set successfully underwent a high-speed trial at 180 kmph on the Mathura–Nagda section on 8 October 2026, under the supervision of the Chief Commissioner of Railway Safety (CCRS).180 kmph speed test for RCF’s Vande BharatThe CCRS inspection assessed the trainset's performance at high speeds, operational efficiency and compliance with safety parameters.Successfully completing the inspection is an important step in the development of advanced Vande Bharat trainsets.Also Read | After launching Vande Bharat sleeper train with 16 coaches, Indian Railways now bets on 24-coach variant of new train with pantry car and features better than Rajdhani ExpressRCF Kapurthala’s production includes coaches for advanced train sets such as Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat.The factory's capabilities have also received international recognition, with its railway coaches being exported to several countries in Asia and Africa. These exports have helped expand India's footprint in the global railway market.RCF Kapurthala recorded its highest-ever annual output in FY 2025–26, manufacturing 2,383 coaches during the year.Vande Bharat ExpressVande Bharat Express, called Train 18 after the year it was manufactured in, was first rolled out in a record time of 18 months. The first Vande Bharat Express was launched in 2019 between Delhi and Varanasi.The fully air-conditioned train set has brought several technological advances to passenger services, opening a new chapter in the country's railway travel experience.Unlike conventional trains that depend on a separate locomotive for traction, the train set can reach speeds of 180 kmph without requiring an engine to pull it.Also Read | Indian Railways exports first 18-coach LHB train for Bangladesh as part of 200 coach order; specially designed coaches feature CCTVs, baby care and prayer rooms, and other passenger-friendly amenitiesOne of the key improvements is its capacity to accelerate and decelerate more rapidly than conventional trains. This capability can reduce journey times by up to 20% across several routes.The train also brings together a range of passenger conveniences and digital features. These include European-style seats, automatic doors, GPS-enabled passenger information systems and onboard infotainment. Its regenerative braking technology helps improve energy efficiency during operation.Semi-permanent couplers are designed to minimise jerks, along with improved suspension systems, help deliver a smoother ride. Regenerative braking also supports more efficient operations by recovering energy as the train slows down.Automatic plug doors and wider, fully sealed gangways allow passengers to move between coaches while creating a more unified structure, instead of treating each coach as an independent unit.Vande Bharat includes provision for KAVACH, India's indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system, which is certified to Safety Integrity Level-4.The trainset has continued to evolve through successive upgrades. The Vande Bharat 3.0 version can go from 0 to 100 kmph in around 52 seconds. It also offers lower levels of noise and vibration, adding to the improvements in its performance and passenger experience.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SpaceX could be worth $50 trillion someday, billionaire investor Ron Baron says
articles.summary: There are Elon Musk bulls on Wall Street, and then there is billionaire investor Ron Baron.
articles.body:
There are Elon Musk bulls on Wall Street, and then there is billionaire investor Ron Baron.

Baron is the founder, chair, and CEO of Baron Capital and a longtime cheerleader of Tesla ( TSLA ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), and Musk. He has never been afraid to make bold calls on the valuations of Musk companies, and today is no exception to his long track record.

In a new interview that just dropped at Columbia Business School, Baron proclaimed that SpaceX could be worth up to $50 trillion in 10 years. Note that SpaceX's current market cap is $2.06 trillion, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.

Here is Baron's latest hot take on SpaceX: "In 10 years, I think it's going to be thousands of dollars a share. I think it'll be worth $20 trillion, $30 trillion, $50 trillion. Elon thinks I'm way low, and it's now $2 trillion. There are good fundamentals, and this is not pulling numbers out of the air. I think Starlink alone, in the next 10 years, is going to be worth somewhere around $14 trillion or $15 trillion, and it's still at the very early stages of that growth. And then the data centers in space—man, that's unbelievable. You can't build them on the planet anymore. How large that business is going to be—it's going to be a multiple of how big Starlink is going to be. We can talk about the fundamentals there later, but the idea is that I'm thinking we're going to make at least 20 or 30 times."

Investing.com -- Fastenal shares slipped about 3% in premarket trading Wednesday after the industrial distributor reported in-line third-quarter results and outlined elevated spending plans for the year.

The company expects 2026 spending on property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales, of $310 million to $330 million, up from $230.6 million in 2025. It cited three factors driving the increase: spending to replace its Atlanta hub and improve picking capacity and efficiency across its hub network, elevated IT spending as delayed projects from 2025 continue through 2026, and higher trucking costs.

Earnings per share for the quarter were $0.35, a penny above the $0.34 analysts expected. Revenue rose 15% from a year earlier to $2.46 billion, ahead of the $2.44 billion consensus. Daily sales were $38.5 million, up 16% and above the $38.1 million estimate.

Operating income climbed 20% to $530.8 million, topping the $512.1 million estimate. Operating margin widened 90 basis points to 21.5%, as leverage on selling, general and administrative costs more than offset gross margin pressure from customer mix. Gross margin was 44.8%, down from 45.3% a year earlier but above the 44.5% analysts expected.

articles.title: IDBI Bank stake sale; Rs 53,428 crore welfare package: Key decisions by Union cabinet
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Union cabinet on Wednesday approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,877 crore and a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Union cabinet on Wednesday approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,877 crore and a five-year extension of national social security schemes with an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore. It also approved a 78-day productivity-linked bonus worth Rs 2,009 crore for railway employees.The decisions cover financial sector restructuring, welfare support for vulnerable sections and festive-season payments for railway workers.The IDBI Bank disinvestment is the largest such exercise since the sale of Air India. The government said the strategic partnership would bring fresh capital into the lender and support the growth of India's financial services sector.The social security package will cover 3.20 crore beneficiaries across all 36 States and Union Territories. It will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 under a revised framework that expands disability pension eligibility and renames several existing welfare schemes.The railway bonus will benefit 11.4 lakh employees ahead of the festive season.IDBI Bank stake sale to bring fresh capitalThe cabinet approved the strategic disinvestment of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,877 crore. The transaction marks a major step in the restructuring of the lender, which has played a significant role in financing India's industrial development.Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the decision was significant for the financial sector, particularly for MSMEs and emerging industries."A major decision has been taken regarding the financial sector, specifically concerning IDBI, an institution crucial for the growth of our MSMEs and new industries. A decision has been made to undertake the strategic restructuring of IDBI," he said.Vaishnaw said India's rapid economic growth had increased the need for capital to help businesses expand."Given the rapid pace of India's growth, there is a significant need for growth capital," he said.He added that the government had selected a strategic partner for IDBI Bank, which has played an important role in India's industrial development."A strategic partner has been selected for the Industrial Development Bank, an institution that has played a pivotal role in industrial development," Vaishnaw said.The partnership, he said, would bring fresh capital into the lender and help attract foreign investment into the financial services sector."This partnership will facilitate the infusion of new capital and pave the way for the largest FDI inflow into India's financial services sector," he said.Vaishnaw said the government and the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) would jointly retain a 34% stake in the restructured entity."The Government of India and LIC will jointly retain a 34% stake in the restructured entity," he said.He added that retaining the stake would increase the value of their holdings."Retaining this 34% stake will significantly enhance the value of the holdings held by both the Government of India and LIC," Vaishnaw said.He described the transaction as an infusion of fresh capital into IDBI Bank and the wider financial services sector."In a sense, fresh capital is being infused into IDBI and the financial services sector," he said.Vaishnaw said the move would create growth opportunities for small businesses, entrepreneurs and companies looking to expand into services."This move will create new growth opportunities, particularly for MSMEs, small industries, new entrepreneurs, and those entering the services sector or looking to expand, while also serving as a major opportunity to attract FDI into financial services," he said.Social security schemes extended for five yearsThe Cabinet also approved a five-year extension of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), with a total outlay of Rs 53,428 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31.The programme will benefit 3.20 crore people across all 36 States and Union Territories. It supports vulnerable households through pension and family assistance schemes, including provisions for senior citizens, widows and people with disabilities.The revised framework includes changes to disability assistance. Disability benefits will now be available from birth, instead of requiring beneficiaries to reach the age of 18. The government has also revised the eligibility criteria, coverage and assistance rates for pensions for persons with disabilities, referred to as Divyangjan.The changes are intended to widen access to support and bring more eligible beneficiaries under the social security framework.Five welfare schemes get new namesAs part of the social security package, the Cabinet approved new names for the NSAP and four of its major schemes. articles.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wealth Arm Brings in Record New Money From IPOs
articles.summary: Morgan Stanley’s profit for the third quarter climbed as the firm’s equity traders trounced analysts’ estimates and the firm’s wealth-management operation br...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Morgan Stanley's profit for the third quarter climbed as the firm's equity traders trounced analysts' estimates and the firm's wealth-management operation brought in a record amount of money.

The stock-trading business generated revenue of $5.8 billion, compared with expectations for $4.9 billion, while the closely watched wealth business soaked up a record $232 billion in net new assets, according to a statement Wednesday.

Morgan Stanley said half of those net new assets were tied to initial public offerings. The firm's IPO bankers have worked on some of the year's biggest listings, including SpaceX. Elon Musk's aerospace company is a customer of Morgan Stanley's workplace channel, which provides clients' employees with benefits like equity compensation, retirement plans and other executive services.

Morgan Stanley and Bank of America Corp. wrapped up third-quarter earnings announcements for the biggest US banks Wednesday in a quarter marked a stark divergence between the performance of equities and fixed-income trading desks. Bond traders are grappling with rising interest rates, which can crimp client activity, while stock traders have notched record after record this year on volatility fueled demand.

In the years following the 2008 financial crisis, Morgan Stanley executives reshaped the firm to focus more on wealth management and less on trading and investment banking. It has swelled into a $8.4 trillion juggernaut in the space, boosted by acquisitions along the way.

Total revenue from the trading operation was $7.81 billion, compared with expectations for $7.31 billion, according to a Wednesday. Wealth management revenue jumped to $9.1 billion from $8.2 billion a year earlier. Net income was $4.97 billion, up from $4.66 billion a year earlier.

Shares of Morgan Stanley, up 5.1% through Tuesday, advanced 0.5% in early New York trading.

Unlike most of its peers, Morgan Stanley's equities business has long been the larger of the two. The firm used to be the biggest stock-trading shop on Wall Street, but Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has claimed that title in recent years.

Morgan Stanley's investment bankers, meanwhile, posted $2.16 billion in net revenue, compared with $2.11 billion a year earlier.

articles.title: Chick-fil-A bet on chicken in the 1960s. Now it’s one of America’s biggest restaurant chains.
articles.summary: The family-owned company reported nearly $24 billion in sales last year and recently expanded to Singapore and the United Kingdom.
articles.body: For decades, Chick-fil-A — with its iconic cow mascot — has encouraged Americans to skip hamburgers and instead “Eat Mor Chikin.” Today Chick-fil-A is the third-largest restaurant chain in the U.S. behind McDonald’s and Starbucks, with nearly $24 billion in sales last year. Chick-fil-A also has around 3,000 locations around the world, having recently expanded to the U.K. and Singapore. But the global giant came from humble beginnings. “My grandfather grew up in extreme poverty,” CEO Andrew Cathy said in a recent interview for NBC News’ Business in America series. “He actually lived in the first government housing in the state of Georgia, and after the war, he decided to start a business with his brother Ben. And they’re like, ‘We want a better life for ourselves,’” Cathy said. So Truett and Ben Cathy opened a diner called the Dwarf Grill in Hapeville, Georgia, in 1946. After a local supplier offered them big chicken breasts that had been rejected by Delta Air Lines, Truett developed the sandwich that eventually became the signature menu item of the first Chick-fil-A restaurant in 1967. Truett’s son Dan Cathy eventually took over the business from his father, and his son Andrew became CEO in 2021. For 60 years, Chick-fil-A has remained a private, family-owned business — and Andrew Cathy says it plans to stay that way. But while much has changed at the company over the decades, its signature chicken sandwich has stayed consistent. “It’s still the same recipe that we’ve had since 1967,” Cathy said. As for what’s in the recipe, he said: “It’s a lot of good things. Can’t tell you the details.” Faith in the business But certainly one of the company’s core ingredients has been the Cathy family’s Christian faith. Chick-fil-A has never been open on Sundays, a decision Cathy said his grandfather and great-uncle made many years ago. “It was very common back in the 1940s that a lot of places were closed on Sunday,” he said. “They wanted to do that. They wanted to have a chance to take a break, go to church and for others just to take some rest.” For the Cathys, the business is an expression of their faith. Chick-fil-A’s mission is to “Glorify God by being a faithful steward of all that is entrusted to us. To have a positive influence on all who come in contact with Chick-fil-A.” But running a business based on Christian values can be challenging in 21st century America. The Cathys experienced that firsthand in 2012, when Dan Cathy told a religious newspaper that the family supported “the biblical definition of the family unit.” Cathy’s comments set off an explosion of controversy when Americans were deeply split over the issue of same-sex marriage. Protests and boycotts of Chick-fil-A restaurants across the country were met with counterprotests and “buycotts.” On Aug. 1 of that year, Chick-fil-A supporters flocked to the restaurant and delivered the company a record-setting “Chick-fil-A Appreciation Day.” The company has also donated millions of dollars to Christian organizations that drew criticism from advocates for LGBTQ+ rights. In 2014, Dan Cathy expressed regret over having involved the company in the debate, although he stood by his private views about marriage. Asked about backlash the company has received on LGBTQ+ issues, Andrew Cathy gave a diplomatic response. “We’ve always been focused on serving great food and hospitality, and so for anybody that comes in the door, we’re going to continue to do that,” he said. The Supreme Court legalized same-sex marriage in 2015, and starting in 2020, Chick-fil-A changed its approach to charitable giving — focusing exclusively on the issues of education, homelessness and hunger. The company’s Shared Table program donates extra food from Chick-fil-A restaurants to local nonprofits that provide meals to people in need. Chick-fil-A says the program has provided more than 200 million meals since 2020. A value proposition The company is also navigating an economic environment this year in which millions of Americans have pulled back on dining out. Consumer prices have jumped 3.4%, while wages have grown just 3% on average — meaning that for many Americans, paychecks aren’t keeping up with rising costs. Chick-fil-A’s prices aren’t the cheapest on the block, either. At a Chick-fil-A in Dallas, for example, the standard chicken sandwich is $4.99. At a McDonald’s less than a mile down the road, the similar McCrispy sandwich costs $3.99. But Cathy said Chick-fil-A knows many of its consumers are feeling pinched and making tough choices about where they want to spend their dollars. “Even though our costs are going up, we’ve got to be careful knowing that consumers are making that trade-off,” he said. “What we want more than anything is if customers do choose to eat with us, they feel like ‘Man, I got a great value for what I paid for this experience.’”

articles.title: Inflation rose to 3.7% last month in last snapshot of consumer prices before the midterms
articles.summary: It’s not just gas.
articles.body: It’s not just gas. It’s the car repair, the doctor’s visit, the plane ticket, the computer upgrade, the new clothes. Inflation rose faster than expected last month, with price pressures extending well beyond the pump, new data showed Wednesday. The latest Consumer Price Index showed that prices rose 0.6% from August, bringing the annual rate of inflation to 3.7%, up from 3.4%, according to new Bureau of Labor Statistics data. Economists were expecting CPI to increase 0.6% on a monthly basis and 3.6% annually. Gas prices, which rose 9.1% in September, accounted for more than half of the monthly increase, according to Wednesday’s report, which is the last look at consumer prices before the midterm elections. “You see the energy crisis causing used car prices to rise, and airfare prices to rise, and recreation costs to rise; and on top of that, you’ve got medical care and apparel also rising,” said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. “So, it’s this more broad-based problem than just a gas price spike.” And the upward trajectory of price hikes is only further compounding affordability concerns for Americans: September marks the sixth month that inflation has wiped out workers’ wage gains. A closely watched gauge of underlying inflation also ran hot last month: Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3% from August and 2.6% from a year earlier. Housing-related inflation, which is captured in the weighty “shelter” category, rose 0.4% from August, the fastest monthly rate in five months, BLS data shows. Shelter-related price hikes have been on a disinflationary path for more than three years; however, economists have questioned how much further those prices could slow as low inventory and high interest rates weigh on the housing industry. Economists were expecting core inflation to slow to 0.2% and for the annual rate to tick up to 2.5% from a five-year low of 2.4%. The energy shock from the Iran war is keeping inflation uncomfortably high, eroding Americans’ pay gains and further compounding affordability concerns. Inflation has now outpaced wage growth for six months in a row. Wednesday’s data puts the Federal Reserve further from its 2% inflation target (measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index) and could prompt policymakers to hike interest rates again if price pressures persist. The broadening of price pressures beyond the pump “bolsters the case for additional rate hikes,” Jeff Schulze, head investment strategist for Franklin Templeton Institute, wrote in a note Wednesday, but noted that recent commentary from Fed officials suggests the bar for such a move could be high when policymakers meet later this month to decide on borrowing costs. Stock futures fell and bond yields surged after the report reinforced traders’ expectations that the Fed will keep interest rates higher for longer to tamp down inflation. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped eight basis points to 5.3%. Odds for a Fed rate hike in October rose to 49% Wednesday morning, up from 22% one day ago, according to CME FedWatch. Traders widely expect the Fed to raise rates at least once before year-end. The US dollar index rose 0.5% and hit its highest level since April 2025. Higher interest rates can boost the dollar. This story is developing and will be updated.

articles.title: Bank of America stock on track for worst day since 2025 as $1.2 billion fine weighs on Q3 earnings
articles.summary: Bank of America said Wednesday that its third quarter profit fell 17% from a year earlier as a $1.2 billion regulatory penalty and a slowdown in its Wall Str...
articles.body:
Bank of America's ( BAC ) stock dropped more than 7% Wednesday, putting shares for the nation's second largest bank on track for its worst single-day move since April 2025 as a $1.2 billion regulatory penalty dragged down results.

The nation's second biggest bank reported third quarter net income of $6.93 billion, or $0.91 per share, compared with the $1.10 per share analysts expected. Excluding the regulatory penalty, Bank of America said it earned $8.1 billion, or $1.08 per share.

Revenue rose 3% to $30 billion, compared with expectations of roughly $30.6 billion.

US regulators charged the Charlotte, North Carolina-based bank $1.2 billion in fines on Tuesday afternoon over widespread failures in the banking giant's safeguards against money laundering and other illicit financial activity

Bank of America's CFO Alastair Borthwick told reporters later Wednesday that much of the spending the bank expects will be needed to fix those failures is already reflected in its operating expenses, as it has already devoted thousands of employees and substantial technological investment to address the regulatory deficiencies.

Borthwick declined to specify when the regulators might formally conclude the remediation process.

Regulatory enforcement orders for major banks can take years. A wider consent order related to a fake account scandal at Wells Fargo lasted for over eight years and included an onerous asset growth restriction on the bank over that period.

During the company's earnings call with analysts, CFO Borthwick clarified that there is no growth restriction with the consent order.

Bank of America's results also offered another glimpse into how America's biggest banks are navigating a quarter with sharply rising borrowing costs, which have supported higher lending income while complicating activity for some of their Wall Street businesses.

"While investment banking and sales and trading revenues were lower, commercial lending grew in every client segment," Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said in a statement with the release.

"Our momentum, reflected in growth in client deposits, wealth flows and consumer activity, supported solid earnings, balance-sheet growth and long-term shareholder value," he added.

Bank of America's net interest income, a core measure for what the bank earns from lending, rose 8% from a year earlier to $16.4 billion, supported by higher loan and deposit balances.

Meanwhile, investment banking fees fell 11% from a year earlier to $1.8 billion while still surpassing analyst forecasts after CEO Moynihan telegraphed the bank's relatively softer period for dealmaking.

articles.title: The S&P 500 is about to break its longest streak without a 1% drop
articles.summary: The S&P 500 has gone 52 trading days without a 1% down day, matching the streak that ended in July 2024.
articles.body:
The stock market keeps on stacking good days only.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) has gone an astonishing 52 trading days without a 1% down day, matching the streak that ended in July 2024, according to research from Global Markets Investor. If the index avoids such a decline in today's session, the streak will become the longest since January 2020, when it lasted 74 trading days.

We say astonishing given the headwinds continuing to be thrown at the market, from elevated inflation to a September interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve to midterm election uncertainty .

No big deal, apparently, as the Teflon market vibes rage on.

Meanwhile, Global Markets Investor noted that the New York Stock Exchange has gone 224 consecutive trading days without a session in which declining stocks accounted for at least 80% of total trading volume, the longest streak since at least 1996. Looked at another way, the market has gone nearly a year without a day of intense, broad-based selling on the NYSE. Investors continue to stay long stocks amid a strong earnings outlook.

S&P 500 third quarter earnings growth is expected to come in at 29.6% year over year.

If 29.6% is the actual growth rate for the quarter, it will mark the third straight quarter of growth above 25%, according to FactSet.

It would also represent the eighth straight quarter of double-digit percentage earnings growth.

For the fourth quarter, Wall Street analysts are calling for earnings growth of 28%.

Analysts are predicting year-over-year earnings growth of 32.7% for 2026. Earnings are seen up 15.6% for 2027.
